[UPDATE 1:06 PM] Examiners were sent underground on manual gas checks, but no mine has come back into production, no examiners' log or posted restart schedule exists, and all three mines remain idle with the atmospheric monitoring link still dark; the safety case for a single-mine restart is started and not finished, so the payroll clock keeps running.

[UPDATE 1:06 PM] The Abingdon center is picking on paper and chain-wide purchase limits are in place, but no published store allocation ranks the six coalfield stores, so resupply still follows whichever manager calls loudest and the stores with nothing stay empty.

[UPDATE 1:06 PM] Food-bank trucks have been committed toward the hollows but no published run schedule exists and no fire hall or church has reported receiving a delivery, so the households an hour from the nearest open store are still waiting and nothing is moving to them this hour.

[UPDATE 1:06 PM] Staples are being bought outside the region against a split funding line and their volumes and arrival times have been published for sites to plan against, but no food-bank truck is running to a fire hall or church in the hollows on any schedule and the faith network's list has not been served; until a distribution reaches those parking lots the households an hour from the nearest open store are still waiting.

[UPDATE 1:06 PM] Fuel, food and medicine are named first on I-81 by a priority order that binds only the carriers who choose to be bound; the idle coal hoppers are being turned toward supply lifts but no published rail schedule is carrying them, so the corridor is ordering traffic it cannot yet guarantee and the left-out carriers are already saying so publicly.

[UPDATE 1:06 PM] No disruption money has been committed this cycle: the Commonwealth's $50K still sits unassigned while only information about who is already receiving cash circulates, so the region still cannot see what the state is not funding and payroll, food, fuel and small-business needs remain unfunded from the only large discretionary pot.

[UPDATE 1:06 PM] Card payments from the region are still slow because out-of-region processors flag every transaction, and the bridge-loan programme remains half-funded with no employer under fifty staff holding a signed, disbursed loan; the employers two payrolls from closing still have nothing in hand and the next payroll date keeps approaching.

[UPDATE 1:06 PM] Paper SNAP and WIC vouchers are accepted in the chain grocers, which keeps some coalfield food purchases moving, but no site has been resupplied with coin or small bills and no local bank is clearing scrip yet, so tills still cannot make change and the cash-and-scrip protocol remains paper only; stations and stores in the hollows will keep turning customers away until change and cash reach the counters.
